results.reader_title: Trade tensions and Brexit challenged Europe’s economic partnerships
results.reader_what: Open-access economics paper analyses US tariff policy, Brexit, the COVID recession and risks to EU multilateral trade.
results.reader_why: US–China confrontation and British withdrawal alter EU access to partners and coordinated economic crisis responses.
results.reader_more: Welfens examines Trump-era tariffs and proposed corrections to optimal-tariff calculations that account for outward foreign investment. He connects US protectionism, Brexit and coronavirus fiscal pressures to reduced international cooperation and suggests EU–ASEAN and broader multilateral engagement. Many outcomes are model-based or projections written in 2020, not observed later history.

deep_analysis.research_question: How did US protectionism, Brexit and pandemic pressures affect European trade and cooperation?
deep_analysis.main_finding: Author finds widening trade-policy conflict and integration stresses for Europe and proposes multilateral economic cooperation.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Original open-access Springer International Economics and Economic Policy article with theoretical calculations and macroeconomic policy discussion.
deep_analysis.qualification: Broad conceptual and model-based essay; pandemic and fiscal forecasts should not be treated as verified realized effects.
deep_analysis.radar_relevance: EU international partnerships, trade conflict exposure and economic-policy sovereignty.
